questions.question: Describe the properties and uses of gold.
questions.expected_answer: Gold is a soft, heavy, bright yellow metal that does not rust or tarnish, can be hammered thin or pulled into wire, and carries electricity very well. It is used for jewellery, as a store of wealth by banks and governments, in cellphones and computers, in dentistry, for medals, and in space to protect visors and satellites.

questions.question: Explain how diamonds form and how they are used.
questions.expected_answer: Diamonds are crystals of pure carbon formed more than a hundred kilometres underground under great heat and pressure, and carried up by volcanic pipes of kimberlite. They are the hardest natural substance. The best are cut and polished into gems for jewellery, while most are used in industry for cutting, drilling, grinding and polishing tools.

questions.question: Name four other minerals mined in South Africa and their uses.
questions.expected_answer: Coal, mined mostly in Mpumalanga, makes most of our electricity and is used for steel, fuel and chemicals. Platinum, from around Rustenburg and Limpopo, cleans car exhaust gases and is used in jewellery and electronics. Iron ore from the Northern Cape makes steel. Chrome makes stainless steel, and copper is used for electrical wires.
